name: Praisenter
shortDescription: A free, open-source church presentation package for Bible verses, song lyrics, media, slides, workspaces and multiple displays.
suitableContexts: Churches seeking a free presentation package
Volunteer teams wanting a simple open-source alternative

pricing.summary: Praisenter states that it is 100% free for any use, with no registration, trial period or limited feature set.

tiers.label: Praisenter
tiers.detail: Supplier states no registration, trial or limited feature set

importExport: Workspace assets can be exported as ZIP files for transfer between computers
Song lyrics can be exported as OpenLyrics or ChordPro; media can be exported in native or raw formats
Bibles, song lyrics and media can be imported into a workspace
support: Project discussion forum and issue tracker

editorial.assessment: Praisenter is a no-cost, open-source choice for core worship presentation. Its suitability depends less on the licence and more on whether the team can rehearse it on the actual service hardware and find the support, Bible translations and content workflow it needs.
bestFor: Cost-conscious churches with basic presentation needs
Teams prepared to rehearse and support an open-source tool
strengths: Free without a time limit or registration
Purpose-built Bible, lyric, media and display workflow
limitations: No commercial support commitment is confirmed
Content licensing and live-service resilience remain the church’s responsibility

procurementVerdict.problem: Cost-conscious churches with basic presentation needs
procurementVerdict.firstCheck: No commercial support commitment is confirmed

longForm.verdict: Praisenter is a practical free alternative for churches that need core Bible, lyric and media presentation without a subscription. It should earn trust through a full service rehearsal, not a feature checklist.

decisionLens.heading: Use the actual Sunday setup to assess a free presenter.
decisionLens.text: A platform can be free but still costly if the team lacks confidence when a projector, display or volunteer hand-off fails. Test the real screens, songs, Bible passages, media, service order and a recovery plan.

sections.heading: Free, open-source presentation
sections.question: Can the volunteer team run it reliably?
paragraphs: Praisenter describes Bible verses, lyrics, videos, slides, templates, workspaces and control of unique content on different displays. It says the software is free for any use without a registration or trial.

Run a rehearsal using licensed content and the church’s ordinary output configuration. Record setup notes for other volunteers and make sure a fallback presentation remains available for early live use.

userFeedback.summary: This profile does not use an independent review score. It is based on Praisenter’s official product and installation information.
themes: The absence of price makes hands-on rehearsal the important evaluation step.
The trade-off is volunteer training and self-managed support.
userFeedback.caveat: Supplier claims are not independent testing, and free presentation software does not include rights to display licensed material.

faq.question: Is Praisenter free?
faq.answer: Yes. Praisenter states that it is 100% free with no registration, trial period or limited feature set.

faq.question: Does Praisenter offer a trial?
faq.answer: No trial is needed because it is free to download and use.

faq.question: Does Praisenter include music or Bible licences?
faq.answer: Not confirmed. Churches remain responsible for appropriate Bible, song and streaming licences.
